quizzes.stem: A service starts Claude's reply with prefilled text on a newly adopted Claude 4.6 model, and every call returns a 400. What is the right recovery?

options.a: Retry each call with exponential back-off and jitter
options.b: Extend the timeout so that each call has longer to finish
options.c: Reword the system prompt so that Claude continues the text
options.d: Rebuild the request so that the user speaks last

explanation.d: The errors page lists the rejected prefill under "Common validation errors": "This model does not support assistant message prefill. The conversation must end with a user message." The module adds that a migration error has the recovery "change the request".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A request that fails the same way every time it is sent is an integration failure until proved otherwise, and retrying it only repeats the failure".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a timeout is the 504 recovery, where the table says "Change the call: stream, or use a batch", while every migration row has the same recovery: "change the request".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "None is cured by a retry, a longer timeout or a different prompt", and a reworded system prompt is a different prompt.

quizzes.stem: A reply to a long-document summary ends mid-sentence, with status 200 and a stop reason of `max_tokens`. What is the origin and the right fix?

options.a: The integration's limit, so raise it or continue the turn
options.b: The model, so reword the prompt to ask for shorter output
options.c: The service, so retry the same call after a short pause
options.d: The account, so ask for a higher quota on the organisation

explanation.a: The table reads `max_tokens` as "Integration: the limit is yours" with the recovery "Raise `max_tokens` or continue the response".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a retry repeats the same limit, and the page says "A cut-off reply is usually your setting".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the trap says "A reply cut by `max_tokens` needs a larger limit or a continuation, and no wording will change it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the status is 200 and no quota was exceeded: stop reasons are "part of the response body" and not account errors.

quizzes.stem: An assistant's reply arrives with status 200 and a stop reason of `refusal`. The team's dashboard shows nothing wrong. What does the documentation imply?

options.a: Nothing failed, so the dashboard is right to show no alert
options.b: A resend will usually work, so the team should retry as is
options.c: Error-rate alerts miss it, so a separate signal is needed
options.d: The service is overloaded, so the call should wait for a header

explanation.c: The page says "Refusals are responses, not errors", so "monitoring built only on error rates won't surface it".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the refusal is a real failure of the request, and the course's advice is to "track refusals as their own signal".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Re-sending a refused request to the same model usually results in another refusal".
explanation.d: Ruled out because waiting for a retry header is the recovery for capacity failures: "Wait for the header, or back off with jitter, then retry", while this reply has status 200.

quizzes.stem: In a trace, the final user entry carried a tool's output and then a line of commentary. The reply came back as `end_turn` with an empty content list. Which diagnosis fits?

options.a: The model chose to stop, so add a user message asking it to continue
options.b: The request layout is at fault, so return the result unaccompanied
options.c: The account reached a limit, so raise the quota before anything else
options.d: The service dropped the output, so retry the same call unchanged

explanation.b: The table says that when text follows the tool result the origin is "The integration: send the tool result alone", and the routine's step 4 says "An `end_turn` with no content blocks is an empty reply. Look at the request before it."
explanation.a: Ruled out because that is the answer only when no text followed: the table gives "The model: add a new user message that asks it to continue" for "If no".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A dropped connection has none: it is the network, and it belongs to the service side", while here a response arrived with a stop reason.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a limit arrives as an error: "An `error` event has one, and the table of page 1 gives its origin and recovery".

quizzes.stem: A team's code could not read this reply: "Sure! Here is the answer: {"label": "spam"} Hope it helps." What does the routine conclude?

options.a: The account lacks access to structured output, so request it
options.b: The model failed to produce JSON, so validate and ask it again
options.c: The service truncated the body, so retry the call with back-off
options.d: The parser was too strict, so pull out the object first

explanation.d: The table says that an object in the text makes it "The integration: the parser was too strict, so extract the object first".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The model: it did not produce JSON, so validate and ask again" applies only when no object is in the text, and here one is.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a cut-off arrives as a stop reason: "A refusal, a `max_tokens` stop, a context-window stop or a pause is a failure of a successful response".
explanation.a: Ruled out because an access failure arrives as an error status: "An `error` event has one, and the table of page 1 gives its origin and recovery".

quizzes.stem: A trace holds a 529, then a retry that returns a good response, then nothing else. What is the finding?

options.a: A service failure, which ended without recovery
options.b: A service failure, which the application survived
options.c: A model failure, which the application survived
options.d: An integration failure, which needs a fix in code

explanation.b: The page says "A 529 is retried and succeeds, so the application recovered", and "A later good response means the failure was survived".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A later good response means the failure was survived", so the trace did recover.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Trace B's 529 is the service's", and a 529 is not model output.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a bug in your request fails the same way each time", while this request succeeded on the retry.

quizzes.stem: A call returns a 429 that carries no `retry-after` header, and its error code says the organisation reached its monthly spend ceiling. What does the module advise?

options.a: Back off with jitter, since capacity frees up within seconds
options.b: Hand it to a person, since only a higher limit or the reset restores access
options.c: Split the work into smaller calls so that each one fits beneath the ceiling
options.d: Move the call to a fallback model, since this one is overloaded

explanation.b: The table sends "Your credential or account (401, 402, 403, a spend cap)" to a person, because "a spend cap lifts only at the monthly reset or with a higher limit", and "No retry can supply a key or a payment".
explanation.a: Ruled out because capacity failures are the ones where you "Wait for the header, or back off with jitter, then retry", and this response has no such header.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the module's rule is to "retry only what can change by itself", and smaller calls do not change an organisation's ceiling.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a fallback model is the recovery for a refusal, where the table says "Use a fallback model, or reset the context", and this is not an overload.

quizzes.stem: After switching the model id, every call returns a 400 whose message says that a forced invocation is not supported for the model. The incident notes list four suspects. Which should the team investigate first?

options.a: The `tool_choice` field that the new release rejects
options.b: The prefilled turn that the new release rejects
options.c: The thinking mode that the new release rejects
options.d: The capacity that the provider holds in that region

explanation.a: The migration table lists `tool_choice` of `any` or a named tool as returning a 400 on Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, with the message "forced tool use is not supported for those models".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the rejected prefill has its own message: "This model does not support assistant message prefill".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a rejected thinking mode is a "400, with a message that points to adaptive thinking and `output_config.effort`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a 400 is a request status and capacity failures are "429 with `retry-after`, 529".

quizzes.stem: A reply ends cleanly with stop reason `end_turn`, but the downstream code throws on it, and the logged output is a sentence followed by a fenced block of JSON. Which statement is true?

options.a: The fault is the integration's parser, so a test should script this sample
options.b: The fault is the service's, so the call should be repeated until it is clean
options.c: The fault is the model's, so the system prompt should forbid code fences
options.d: The fault is the integration's limit, so `max_tokens` should be raised

explanation.a: The table says an object between the first `{` and the last `}` makes it "The integration: the parser was too strict, so extract the object first", and the page says to prove a fix "with a test that scripts the trace".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the trap warns "Assuming the model when the output is odd", and the output does hold the JSON.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the module's rule is to "retry only what can change by itself", and a repeat gives the same shape.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a limit shows as a cut-off: "A reply that stops mid-sentence with status 200 is the integration's configuration", while this reply ends cleanly with `end_turn`.

quizzes.stem: A bug in a tool-use loop is fixed in production on a Friday evening. Which follow-up does the module recommend?

options.a: Close the incident, since the fix was deployed
options.b: Add a note to the runbook and rely on the next on-call
options.c: Scrub the trace and add it to the eval set as a case
options.d: Lower the retry budget so that the failure is less visible

explanation.c: The page says "A trace that went wrong in production is the best test case you will ever get: scrub it, give it an id and a tag, and add it to the eval set or the test suite."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A bug that is fixed without a test or an eval case will return", as the last trap puts it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a runbook note records the bug and does not test for it, and the page says "The bug cannot return unseen" once it is a case.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a smaller budget hides failures, while the routine says to "note whether the application recovered".
